text:
jordan: quick heads-up — ran into a weird edgecase in the billing stitcher today. cross-tenant request (shared prompt from integration) produced credits for two tenants but only one claim showed up in ledger. wondering best approach for attributing the leftover tokens for billing and audits

marta: can you paste the raw event? is this before or after enrichment?

jordan: it hit proxy -> enrich -> fanout. enrich added tenant=A, but the downstream model call returned provenance that included tenant=B in the metadata (shared user session). final billing event only had tenant=A per current handshake logic

sam: hmm. two immediate options: 1) tag requests early with multi-tenant envelope and carry list through (slower, larger payloads) 2) create a post-hoc stitcher that scans provenance and emits additional billing claims (async, harder to prove determinism)

lee: tradeoff feels familiar. early tag = accurate real-time attribution but increases token of record size and touches all paths. post-hoc stitching = smaller impact on latency, but then you need strong idempotency and deterministic ordering for the audit ledger

marta: for audits we need an immutable chain — if we emit an extra claim later, auditors will want a clear provenance pointer to the original request. that means the stitcher must emit links: original_event_id + stitch_reason. is that feasible?

sam: yes feasible. we'd add fields like original_event_id and stitched_by_job_id. but then how do we guarantee you can't double-count if the original claim gets reprocessed? need a dedupe key based on fingerprint + stitch_reason

natalie: also factor in billing windows and SLA. customers expect usage in the same billing period. If stitcher runs after close, it either shifts charges to next invoice or we need a late-adjustment flow + notification

jordan: good point. can we bound the stitcher window? e.g., keep a 24h reconciliation window for late claims and anything past that becomes a manual audit adjustment?

lee: 24h window seems reasonable for most customers. for enterprise SLAs maybe allow configurable grace windows per tenant. also: what about cost allocation when both tenants share a single model call? do we split tokens or choose primary tenant?

sam: allocation strategies: 1) primary-tenant wins (simpler) 2) proportional split by usage markers (hard) 3) credit-sidecar that mints synthetic credits and maps later during reconciliation. each has accounting complexity

marta: my leaning: default to primary-tenant for low friction, provide opt-in proportional allocation for accounts that need it. document the guarantees clearly

natalie: need UX for opt-in. billing console should show stitched adjustments, original_event_id, and who paid what. also notifications when late stitching causes > $X delta

lee: on implementation: propose we add a lightweight provenance envelope at proxy level with fields: tenant_hints[], original_request_fingerprint. Pass through to model runtime but keep it minimal. Have stitcher read model provenance and emit 'stitch_claim' events with dedupe_key = sha256(fingerprint|stitch_reason|target_tenant)

jordan: sample dedupe pseudo:
```
dedupe_key = sha256(fingerprint + 'stitch' + target_tenant)
if not seen(dedupe_key): emit_claim(...)
```

sam: also recommend instrumenting a metric: stitched_claims_by_delay_bucket and expose it in console. that will guard us against surprise late-bill spikes

marta: agree. last question: do we need to change the ledger schema? adding stitched_by and original_event pointer probably sufficient, no need for full rewrite

billing-bot: Background job "stitcher-v2" scheduled to run at 2024-06-10T06:00:00Z :white_check_mark:

jordan: OK, action items: 1) add provenance envelope to proxy (lee) 2) add dedupe_key and stitched_by fields to claim schema (sam) 3) reconcile window + opt-in policy docs (marta/natalie) 4) instrument stitched_claims metrics (lee/sam). I'll open a quick RFC with the above and link it here. :thumbsup:

marta: thanks — please tag me on the RFC for opt-in UX notes

sam: i'll prototype dedupe lib and a small integration test for double-process scenarios

lee: i'll sketch the minimal envelope and perf impact numbers, ping if you want numbers for a 1% payload overhead vs baseline

jordan: awesome — closing the loop, will post RFC link in this thread later.
